evidence.policy: Evidence is scored in three views. (1) Pooled: micro-aggregated true/false-positive/negative counts over every parsed record, identical to the headline metric in eval/metrics.py. Records with no annotated gold evidence cannot add recall and any cited sentence on such a record counts as a false positive. (2) Gold-present: the same scoring restricted to records whose gold evidence set is non-empty; the primary comparable retrieval number. (3) Per-record: every gold-present record contributes one P/R/F1 triple and the macro average is reported. Records with empty gold evidence are reported separately as a consistency rate (predicted evidence also empty); they never earn credit toward evidence quality. Empty predicted evidence is always measured, never treated as proof of eligibility or ineligibility, by the analysis or the report.

evidence.policy: Evidence is scored in three views. (1) Pooled: micro-aggregated true/false-positive/negative counts over every parsed record, identical to the headline metric in eval/metrics.py. Records with no annotated gold evidence cannot add recall and any cited sentence on such a record counts as a false positive. (2) Gold-present: the same scoring restricted to records whose gold evidence set is non-empty; the primary comparable retrieval number. (3) Per-record: every gold-present record contributes one P/R/F1 triple and the macro average is reported. Records with empty gold evidence are reported separately as a consistency rate (predicted evidence also empty); they never earn credit toward evidence quality. Empty predicted evidence is always measured, never treated as proof of eligibility or ineligibility, by the analysis or the report.

examples.criterion: 13. Evidence of uterine pathology other than leiomyoma
examples.note:
0. A 36-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with 12 weeks of amenorrhea, vaginal spotting that has increased since yesterday, lower abdominal tenderness, nausea and vomiting.
1. The physical exam reveals overall tender abdomen, 18-week sized uterus, and cervical dilation of 2 cm.
2. The complete blood count and biochemical profile are normal.
3. Point of care pregnancy test with cut-off sensitivity of 25 mIU/ml Beta-HCG is negative.
4. The ultrasound reports enlarged uterus (12 cm x 9 cm x 7 cms) with multiple cystic areas in the interior.
5. The differential diagnosis includes vesicular mole vs fibroid degeneration.
6. The patient will provide informed consent, and will comply with the trial protocol without any practical issues.

evidence.policy: Evidence is scored in three views. (1) Pooled: micro-aggregated true/false-positive/negative counts over every parsed record, identical to the headline metric in eval/metrics.py. Records with no annotated gold evidence cannot add recall and any cited sentence on such a record counts as a false positive. (2) Gold-present: the same scoring restricted to records whose gold evidence set is non-empty; the primary comparable retrieval number. (3) Per-record: every gold-present record contributes one P/R/F1 triple and the macro average is reported. Records with empty gold evidence are reported separately as a consistency rate (predicted evidence also empty); they never earn credit toward evidence quality. Empty predicted evidence is always measured, never treated as proof of eligibility or ineligibility, by the analysis or the report.
